reply.subject: GSS_PowerStrip

observed.facings.png: One top-down view of a long, thin, rounded-corner bar in warm beige/light grey plastic with a faint mottled texture and a dark outline. Four evenly spaced round black sockets with two pin holes each (Euro/Schuko style) run along it, and a small glowing orange-red rocker switch sits at the right end. Clean transparent background. No cord, stub or tail anywhere.
observed.south.png: The same strip at native 256x128. The bar fills most of the width (about x 12–232), with a slightly larger empty margin on the right than the left. It is vertically centred, about 44 px tall. The switch is lit orange-red. The edges are crisp, with no halo.
observed.scale.png: A comparison composite on a flat brown floor, at 64 px/cell (top row) and 128 px/cell (bottom row). BEFORE is the old low-res grey strip, with a small dark stub at its right end feeding the cord. AFTER lit and AFTER off show the new beige strip: two orange extension cords come down from above and their plug heads land on sockets 1 and 3, and the orange feed cord leaves the right end cap horizontally. The new strip reads clearly at 64 px/cell, and the stub is gone.
observed.variants_1.png: The off variant, identical to south.png except that the rocker switch is a dark unlit maroon. Same body, sockets and palette.
observed.assembled_1.png: Close-up composite of the lit strip on a flat brown floor. Two orange cords with tan rectangular plug heads come from the top; their heads draw over the strip and end over the upper half of sockets 1 and 3, leaving the lower half of each socket visible. Sockets 2 and 4 are empty. The feed cord meets the right end cap at the bar's mid-height and runs off to the right. The switch glows. The flat untextured floor suggests an offline composite rather than a live game capture.
observed.assembled_2.png: The same composite with the off variant: the switch is dark and everything else is identical to assembled_1.

CAMERA.seen: A floor decal drawn flat and top-down, which is the engine limit for this subject (no 35-degree building camera applies). The bar has no false perspective.

BORE.seen: The texture contains no pipe or hose, so no open bore is shown anywhere. The code-drawn cords in the assembled views show no bore either.

PORTS.seen: In assembled_1/2 the feed cord meets the right end cap at the bar's mid-height, and both plug heads sit over sockets 1 and 3 at the socket x-positions. The heads cover only the upper half of each socket (polish, noted as a finding).

LAYERS.seen: The plug heads draw over the strip and the feed cord abuts the end cap from underneath/behind, as the description specifies.

ROTATIONS.seen: A single top-down picture. The lit and off variants have the same body, sockets and palette; only the switch glow differs.

SIGNATURE.seen: Four dark sockets along the bar, a rocker switch at the right end, and a beige plastic body. It reads instantly as a power strip.

MATERIAL.seen: A slightly mottled warm beige with subtle edge shading reads as moulded plastic. The sockets read as black plastic inserts and the switch as a translucent lit rocker.

FOOTPRINT.seen: The bar sits inside the 256x128 canvas with small margins and nothing is cropped. The right margin (~24 px) is a little larger than the left (~12 px), and the composites show it meeting the feed cord correctly.

ALPHA.seen: A clean transparent background with no shadow, halo or ground patch around the bar.

OURS.seen: A new painterly strip in the Modern look, clearly different from the old 64x32 grey texture shown as BEFORE; nothing suggests donor art.

OWNER_NOTES.seen: The resolution is much higher (256x128, crisp sockets) and no wire, stub or tail is baked in. In the composites the code-drawn plugs land on the sockets and the feed cord ends at the cap, which is the 'one cable ends in a power strip that other cables plugged into' look the owner asked for.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 64 px/cell in scale.png the beige bar, dark socket dots and red switch still read. At 32 px/cell it becomes a ~29x5 px light bar with dark dots, which is enough for a small floor decal.

reply.needs_call_why: The assembled panels look like an offline composite (flat untextured floor, scale.png captioned as a built comparison) rather than a live in-game capture. PORTS and LAYERS were therefore judged on a mock, and a second reviewer may want to confirm the plug-head offsets against the C# placement.
proposals: The code-drawn plug heads are rectangular blade-style plugs while the strip's sockets are round two-pin Euro sockets. Matching socket shape to plug type (or the reverse) would make 'plugged in' read more precisely when zoomed in.

For floor decals (no facings, top-down by engine limit), give the machine template a `decal` module that skips CAMERA, BORE and ROTATIONS, so reviewers are not pushed to stretch building-camera questions onto a flat decal.

reply.image_seen: Image 1 shows an enlarged beige four-socket bar with a lit switch; image 2 shows the isolated lit texture; image 3 compares old and candidate cord connections at two scales; image 4 shows the dark switch variant; images 5 and 6 show two orange plugs overlapping the bar and a feed cord meeting its right end.

concerns.evidence: In both assembled panels, the brown plug heads cover the upper portions of sockets 1 and 3 but terminate above their centres. The exposed dark socket portions extend below the heads, making the heads appear displaced north of their insertion points.

The transparent margins are slightly unequal, but the isolated bar spans most of the canvas width, remains fully contained, and has substantial readable detail. It neither overflows its footprint nor floats tiny inside the canvas; the margin difference does not establish a FOOTPRINT defect.

request.subject: GSS_PowerStrip

edits.change: The four sockets are each a single dark rectangular face with a thin lighter bezel, and each socket's visual centre sits exactly on its slot position along the strip's long centre line, at even spacing.

Each socket is small and compact (about one quarter of the strip's length wide, and no taller than two thirds of the strip's width), centred on the strip's mid-line, so a plug head centred on it fully covers the socket face from above with a margin of bezel all round.

The socket faces are flat and seen straight from above, with no deep recess, no inner shadow that extends past the bezel, and no lower lip, so nothing of the socket remains visible once a plug head sits on its centre.

invariants: Flat top-down view on a transparent background, no cast shadow
Overall proportion 2:1 (0.9 x 0.45 cells), long axis horizontal, readable at small size
Four sockets in one row with equal spacing along the long axis, each centred on the strip's mid-line
Right end cap is a plain rounded cap where the feed cord enters, with no cord drawn in the sprite
Rocker switch on the strip body clear of the sockets, glowing warm amber-green in the lit variant and unlit dull grey in the Off variant
Same body, socket layout and outline in both variants, only the rocker switch glow differs
Painterly vanilla RimWorld style, realistic, clean dark outline
request.prompt: Top-down view of a floor power strip for a RimWorld sprite, drawn flat on a transparent background, painterly vanilla RimWorld style, realistic, clean dark outline, no cast shadow. The strip is a slim rounded rectangle with a 2:1 length-to-width proportion, long axis horizontal, in worn off-white or pale grey plastic with a subtle highlight along the upper edge and soft shading toward the lower edge. Four identical sockets sit in one evenly spaced row along the strip's long centre line, each socket a small compact dark rectangular face about one quarter of the strip's length wide and no more than two thirds of the strip's width tall, with a thin lighter bezel around it. Each socket's centre lies exactly on the strip's mid-line at its slot position; the socket faces are flat and seen straight from above, with matte dark interior, no deep recess, no inner shadow reaching beyond the bezel, and no lower lip, so a plug head centred on the socket covers its whole face with a margin of bezel all round. The right end cap is a plain rounded cap, clear of any cord, where a feed cord enters. A small rocker switch sits on the strip body in the free space beside the sockets, clear of them. Lit variant: the rocker switch glows warm amber-green with a soft small halo on the plastic around it. Off variant: identical strip with the rocker switch unlit, dull grey. Body, socket layout and outline are identical in both variants; only the rocker switch differs. Crisp readable shapes at small size, transparent background.
